title: Lahaina Disaster Recovery Update Meeting: December 6, 2023

recap.headline: Lahaina recovery update: housing, debris removal timeline, temporary school and loans
recap.in_60_seconds: Maui County, federal and state agencies gave their weekly Lahaina recovery update at a community gym, with staff staying afterward to answer individual questions at tables. No residents testified from the floor; about a dozen officials and community partners presented. The Mayor said a council measure offering tax waivers to owners who rent units to fire survivors passed and faces final reading next week, aiming for 2,700 to 3,000 units. Reentry ends next Tuesday, debris removal is set to start mid-January, the temporary King Kamehameha III Elementary is due within 95 days of November 20, and the FEMA aid deadline is December 11, with SBA loan applications accepted until January 25. Unresolved items include sewer service for Wahikuli and standing burn-zone homes, the Olowalu debris site transfer, and release of ash test results.

parts.title: Welcome and goals for the night
presented: Housing is the community's top concern; partners will give updates
More help on mental health and wellness is being arranged with partner groups
Staff will be at tables after presentations to handle individual situations privately

parts.title: Lahaina advisory team and rental tax incentive
parts.presenter: Mayor and a member of the Lahaina advisory team
presented: The community advisory team grew to six members, one for each of six recovery areas: cultural and natural resources, well-being, infrastructure and housing, economic recovery, community planning, and a Filipino community resource center
The team meets Monday and Friday evenings and attends the weekly meetings to carry community concerns to agencies
Launiupoko Beach reopened after Parks crews removed debris
A council measure to waive taxes for owners who make short-term rentals, timeshares or second homes available to survivors passed and has final reading next week, targeting 2,700 to 3,000 units

next.what: Final council reading of the rental tax waiver measure

parts.title: Emergency management transition and long-term recovery group
parts.presenter: Acting administrator, Maui Emergency Management Agency; Hawaiʻi Community Foundation representative
presented: The former MEMA administrator's 90-day contract ended; an acting administrator now leads
Reentry ends next Tuesday, closing the response phase and moving work to the recovery office
A community-led long-term recovery group is being set up with state and county help; people can sign up at the foundation's table

next.what: Reentry ends and response phase closes

parts.title: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers: debris removal and temporary school
parts.presenter: Commander, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Recovery Field Office
presented: Phase 1 site assessments continue with cultural monitors on each parcel
Debris removal in Lahaina is set to start mid-January, depending on rights of entry and finishing the debris storage site
Notice to proceed on the temporary King Kamehameha III Elementary was issued November 20, with 95 days to deliver; modular units are arriving
Goal is for students to be back in the school after spring break this academic year

next.what: Start of debris removal in Lahaina

next.when: 95 days from November 20; students back after spring break

parts.title: EPA: hazardous materials and water systems
parts.presenter: EPA incident commander for hazardous materials removal; EPA water division director
presented: Phase 1 hazardous materials removal is complete in Upcountry and Lahaina, but buried hazards and physical hazards remain; residents should follow precautions
Soil stabilizer work has about a week left; EPA hazmat teams demobilize by December 21
At its peak the team had 250 members, over half from Maui and Lahaina
EPA will help the County camera-inspect sewer pipes starting as soon as mid-January, for about a month

next.what: EPA hazmat teams complete and demobilize
Camera inspection of damaged sewer lines
next.when: as soon as mid-January, about one month

parts.title: Public Works: stormwater controls during the Kona storm
parts.presenter: County highways chief and Lahaina Highways supervisor
presented: Crews inspected and adjusted erosion controls in the burn zone and added 1,500 feet of new controls, including at Mala
The controls worked as designed during the storm and kept 11 cubic yards of material out of the ocean
The Mayor thanked the Lahaina Highways supervisor for helping evacuate the gym shelter to Kapalua on August 8

parts.title: Environmental Management: wastewater and debris site
parts.presenter: Director, County Department of Environmental Management
presented: After a three-hour meeting with federal and state partners, the County is looking at sewering Wahikuli if possible, with no promises
Standing burn-zone homes can reconnect only after sewer line damage is found and cleared
The Lahaina treatment plant is still fragile from saltwater and ash intrusion and serves about half of West Maui customers
The state granted a right of entry for the Olowalu debris site; an executive order from the governor would transfer management

parts.title: State Department of Health: lead screening, ash results, air sensors
parts.presenter: Deputy Director for Environmental Health, State Department of Health
presented: A lead screening van, with flu and COVID shots, is being arranged for this community center
Lahaina ash sample results came back and will be released by press release
Clean Water Branch found the erosion controls look good
Five more air sensors were installed, for 25 in Lahaina, with more coming

parts.title: FEMA housing and SBA loans
parts.presenter: FEMA Region 9 Administrator; SBA Office of Disaster Recovery and Resilience representative
presented: FEMA has given housing aid to almost 4,000 people, 3,700 with rental aid raised to 175% of fair market rent, but only about 200 have used it to rent
About 1,500 people need direct housing; FEMA is leasing units (about 200 so far) and designing temporary units on three or four County-identified sites
FEMA aid deadline is December 11; those with insurance living expenses are urged to rent now
SBA will take disaster loan applications 45 days after the deadline, until January 25, with no explanation needed; accepting a loan is optional

next.what: FEMA industry day with rental owners and managers
SBA disaster loan applications accepted without extra documents

parts.title: Closing and agency tables
presented: Latest updates are at mauirecovers.org
The emergency management administrator search drew 16 applications, narrowed to five
Agencies stayed at tables for questions, including on debris sites

answered.said: The former administrator leads the hiring team; 16 applied, five remain, and interviews are being worked on now.

next.what: Hiring of a permanent emergency management administrator

bills.name: Rental tax waiver measure for owners housing survivors
bills.what: Waives taxes for owners who make short-term rentals, timeshares or second homes available to displaced fire survivors.

bills.name: Olowalu debris site right of entry
bills.what: State land board right of entry letting the County temporarily manage Olowalu land for permanent debris disposal until a governor's executive order transfers management.

open_questions.question: Will Wahikuli be connected to the County sewer system, and when?
When can standing homes in the burn zone reconnect to sewer service?
When will the governor's executive order transfer the Olowalu debris site to the County?
What did the Lahaina ash samples show?
Where and when will FEMA's temporary housing units open?

not_on_tracker.why: Residents have questions and confusion about where Lahaina's fire debris will be stored for good.
